Sensors._comment_imu: BMI088-class noise model (the unit on the real IFS-08). Datasheet noise densities: accel 175 µg/√Hz, gyro 0.014 °/s/√Hz. At 400 Hz sample rate (200 Hz Nyquist BW) those become ~0.024 m/s² and ~0.0035 rad/s per-sample standard deviations. Bias drift is modelled as Ornstein–Uhlenbeck with a 100 s correlation time, a typical bench-test characteristic for a MEMS IMU at FS race-car operating temperatures.

Lidar1._comment_lidar: Hesai ATX_S01 datasheet (Section 1.4): 1-D rotating mirror (hybrid solid-state), 116 ch, 120° H × 18.3° V FoV (-12.4° to +5.9°), 10 Hz, ~1.74 M pts/s @ 0.08° H, 3 cm 1σ range. PointsPerSecond bumped from 500 k → 1.74 M (datasheet rate) once the LiDAR stream moved off TCP onto the new UDP transport (LIDAR_TRANSPORT=udp in docker-compose.yml). On TCP at 1.74 M pts/s the bridge dropped to ~3 Hz on macOS Docker Desktop because of its TCP loopback throughput cap; the UDP path (chunked, paced, with a Fast DDS-friendly bridge reassembly) holds ~7-8 Hz at the full datasheet rate. The remaining gap to the nominal 10 Hz is now in the DDS layer (1.4 MB BEST_EFFORT messages fragment-loss between publisher and subscriber) — tracked as a follow-up. Sensor packs only emit *hits*, so the wire rate is roughly 65 % of attempted rays (e.g. 1.14 M pts/s of valid range returns at 1.74 M attempted).
Lidar1._comment_maxrange: MaxRange in metres. Real Hesai ATX_S01 spec is 200 m. Set to 30 m for the sim because cones past 30 m don't matter for FS detection (max-corridor-width is well under that), and shrinking the per-ray broadphase distance is the cheapest UE5 CPU optimisation we have — Chaos walks the spatial hash for every actor along the ray's path, so a 7× shorter ray cuts the per-ray work by roughly that factor. Bump back to 200 for benchmarks against real-car captures or non-FS scenarios.
Lidar1._comment_mount: Mount aligned with the IFS-08's actual LiDAR position: X=0 (CoG-aligned, just beneath the main hoop), Y=0 (centered), Z=1.10 m (main hoop crossbar height). Previously X=0.5 m / Z=0.9 m was a hood-mount approximation; correcting it shifts the sensor back ~50 cm and up ~20 cm, which changes both the cone-detection range envelope (cones at the rear become visible) and the time-to-first-detection for cones immediately ahead. Verify cone_detection still classifies cluster heights correctly after re-baselining.
Lidar1._comment_lidarpath: GPU path active (#223 Phase 1). Renders depth at the LiDAR's spherical scan envelope; produces NO point cloud yet — Phases 2-3 add async readback + decode shader. The /lidar/Lidar1 topic will be empty under this setting until Phase 3 lands. Switch back to 'cpu' to restore live point clouds.
